minutes.headline: School choice for the high school was tabled; the FY20 school gap could mean about nine positions cut.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a blizzard bag pilot proposal and asked for more research on other districts and union impact before approving anything. what_happened.line: The committee tabled the school choice decision for the high school; the superintendent is to return at the first March meeting with staffing cuts and a school choice number by grade.
The business manager said the gap between the FY20 guideline and the proposed budget would mean roughly nine full-time equivalent positions.
The committee heard a blizzard bag pilot proposal and referred it for more research on other districts and union impact, with no vote.
The committee authorized the chair to send feedback to the land use director on school setbacks in the cannabis bylaw.
The committee approved the 2019-2020 school calendar with the last day of school pushed back one day, and approved the line transfers as outlined.

why_it_matters: If the FY20 gap holds, about nine school positions could be cut, which would touch class sizes and services, and school choice seats are one way the district may try to offset that.
Where cannabis businesses may sit near schools and playgrounds is being set in a town bylaw, so the committee's feedback feeds into a rule residents may be asked to vote on.
Blizzard bags would change how snow days are handled, but food service pay and other contract terms would need bargaining first.
